Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Trade and Industry budget

Committee of Supply2 March 2026 budget-2894

A Committee of Supply debate on Head V of the Ministry of Trade and Industry's budget, opened by a proposed $100 reduction and followed by Members' cuts and ministerial responses.

The debate covers MTI's budget and policy directions, including support for SMEs, internationalisation, energy, and consumer protection. It records that public consultations on consumer protection will begin on 16 March 2026, and that the Government will reassess GDP and inflation forecasts if necessary. The record does not state that the specific proposals raised by Members were adopted.

Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Education budget

Committee of Supply2 March 2026 – 3 March 2026 budget-2896, budget-2902

A Committee of Supply debate on Head K, the Ministry of Education, with Members moving cuts and the Minister and Ministers of State responding.

The debate records changes to primary and secondary education, including the GEP refresh, a single Post-Secondary Admissions Exercise from 2028, Higher Mother Tongue eligibility from Secondary 1, and more financial assistance for lower- to middle-income students from Academic Year 2026. It also records reviews of Primary 1 registration, class sizes, milestone exams and DSA, and a salary review for educators.

Committee of Supply debate on MDDI Head Q: AI adoption, online safety and cybersecurity

Committee of Supply2 March 2026 budget-2895

A Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Digital Development and Information's Head Q budget, opened by Mr Sharael Taha moving a $100 reduction and followed by ministerial responses.

The debate covers measures intended to help more local enterprises adopt AI, with the National AI Impact Programme aiming to support 10,000 local enterprises over three years. It also covers online safety, scam and misinformation risks, and a planned AI translation tool to make public-facing materials more accessible to non-English speakers. The record does not quantify the effect on households or individual workers beyond these stated aims.

  • Mr Sharael Taha

    • Mr Sharael Taha moved to reduce the Head Q allocation by $100.

      Verbatim17 words
      That the total sum to be allocated for Head Q of the Estimates be reduced by $100

Ministry of Law Committee of Supply debate and vote on a $100 budget cut

Committee of Supply27 February 2026 – 2 March 2026 budget-2886, budget-2888, budget-2893

A Committee of Supply debate on the Ministry of Law's budget, including a proposed $100 reduction moved by Mr Vikram Nair, which was put to a vote.

The debate sets out plans to expand civil legal aid to more households, with the per capita household income threshold rising from $1,050 to $1,650 and the savings threshold from $10,000 to $12,000, targeted for later this year. It also covers reforms to civil judgment enforcement, including new Civil Judgment Enforcement Officers, with a Bill planned later this year. The proposed $100 reduction to the Ministry of Law's budget was put to a vote and the 'Noes' had it.

  • Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)

    • Mr Vikram Nair moved a reduction of $100 to Head R of the Estimates.

      Verbatim19 words
      I move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head R of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

  • The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)

    • MinLaw will review key legislation this year, including arbitration, corporate insolvency and IP.

      Verbatim12 words
      This will include, this year, reforms in arbitration, corporate insolvency and IP.

      Verbatim11 words
      We will raise the means-test criteria to a PCHI of $1,650.

      Verbatim12 words

      Verbatim36 words

What happens next The proposed $100 reduction was put to a vote and the "Noes" had it, so the reduction was not agreed. The Ministry will proceed with the plans announced, including the civil legal aid expansion targeted for later this year and a Bill on civil judgment enforcement later this year.

How this page was made

Built from the official Hansard record (Parliament of Singapore Official Reports). No news reporting was used. Briefs are written by software from the transcript and every key point carries the verbatim words it was drawn from.

  • Reports collected: 65 (complete)
  • Briefs on this page: 4 (159 verified points)
  • Speaker attribution: 98% of turns carry an explicit speaker tag
  • Any point whose quote could not be found in the transcript was discarded rather than shown.
